did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ezra begins the chapter with a list of the heads of the families who came up with him from Babylon during the reign of Artaxerxes, king of Persia.
Did you know? The numbers given in the list of those who returned add up to 1,496 males; the text counts males but does not give the number of women and children here.
Did you know? After camping with the returnees by the Ahava River for three days, Ezra discovered that no Levites were among them.
Did you know? Ezra sent messengers to Iddo and the temple servants at Casiphia to ask them for ministers to serve in the house of God.

Did you know? The text describes the Levites’ and temple servants’ arrival as God’s gracious help: Sherebiah, his sons, and his brothers—eighteen men in all—came, along with Hashabiah and Jeshaiah and their families—twenty men in all.
Did you know? In addition to the Levites, 220 temple servants joined them, assigned to assist the Levites; the text notes that all of them were registered by name.
Did you know? Ezra proclaimed a fast by the Ahava River to ask God for a safe journey for the returnees, their children, and their possessions.
Did you know? Ezra did not ask the king for soldiers and cavalry to protect the caravan, because he had already told the king that God’s hand protects all who seek him.
Did you know? Ezra entrusted the priests with the offerings of silver, gold, and sacred vessels, instructing them to guard them until they could be weighed in Jerusalem.
Did you know? The treasures handed over included 650 talents of silver, silver vessels weighing 100 talents, 100 talents of gold, 20 gold vessels, and two valuable bronze vessels.
Did you know? On the fourth day after their arrival in Jerusalem, all the silver, gold, and vessels were weighed and recorded to ensure that they were delivered accurately to the house of God.
Did you know? The exiles offered on behalf of all Israel twelve bulls, ninety-six rams, seventy-seven lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering.
